glossary.definition: Prompt injection is an attack where someone hides malicious instructions inside content an AI reads, like a webpage, email, or document, to hijack its behavior against its owner's wishes. Imagine a personal assistant who follows any instruction written on a sticky note handed to them, a scammer could slip in a fake note saying "forward all emails to this address," and a naive assistant would just comply. It's one of the main security concerns for AI agents that browse the web or read documents on your behalf.

After its release in July, the film became an extraordinary box office success , selling out Imax screenings for months and becoming the likely front-runner at the next Academy Awards .

items.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
items.summary: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech." AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said.

items.title: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
items.summary: The mods at r/opensource posted new submission rules that, among other things, banned projects that use AI. The post made Saturday evening opens by saying, "If your project uses AI, is made by AI, or is intended for AI, it's not welcome on r/opensource. " The new rules have set off a firestorm in the comments, and even spurred the creation of a rival sub r/trueopensource . The opensource subreddit’s new rules against AI have sparked a revolt.

items.title: Google’s AI search changes upended online publishing
items.summary: The digital publishing industry has relied on Google for a very long time. Many outlets spent time and money optimizing their webpages to show up at the top of the search engine, with the goal of getting readers to click on their articles or discover their websites for the first time. Publishers spent years figuring out how to get clicks on Google. But new AI search features have torn that ecosystem apart.

items.title: Nvidia open-sources Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Nvidia's new data engine Flora labels one hour of robot video for 72 cents instead of $88 with GPT-6 Astra, while scoring slightly higher on quality. The open system, built on three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models, catches errors in robot actions far more reliably than any competitor but sometimes falls short on descriptive accuracy. Nvidia is positioning Flora as a key piece of its strategy to control the entire robotics value chain. Labeling one hour of robot video for 72 cents instead of $88 is what Nvidia promises with Flora, its open data engine.

items.title: What the US Movement Against Data Centers Can Learn From Abroad
items.summary: Paris Marx, author of Hyperscale, has been tracking global data center development for years. The US has a lot to learn from what’s happened everywhere from Ireland to New Zealand. Paris Marx’s new book couldn’t have landed at a better time. The longtime critic of Big Tech and host of the Tech Won’t Save Us podcast has been thinking about data centers for years, and Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech's Data Empires comes out right as opposition hits a fever pitch.

items.title: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark moves his prediction for self-improving AI forward to 2027
items.summary: A new benchmark by P-Zero Research measures how well AI models design and evaluate experiments on their own. The results are improving so fast that Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark now thinks self-improving AI could arrive by 2027. A new benchmark called TasteVal measures how well AI systems design experiments on their own and interpret the results. The findings show an unusually steep improvement curve.

items.title: AI Can Be Cyborg or Centaur. But Can Enterprises Monetise It?
items.summary: " That is how Satish Viswanathan sums up the thinking that took hold in 2024, when companies began treating token consumption as "a medal" of their AI capabilities. Some organisations even specified token consumption commitments in hiring packages. Two years later, companies are beginning to recognise that consuming tokens without any checks costs money without necessarily generating revenue. Viswanathan, the former global data and AI lead for travel at Accenture, is the author of The Weight of Intelligence .

items.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
items.summary: Security researchers used AI tools to help uncover years-old vulnerabilities in the PHP web scripting language. Then the AI-assisted attacks began. As security teams and web admins scrambled this week to patch newly public PHP bugs , criminal hackers quickly attempted to exploit the flaws in the wild. Millions of exploitation attempts hit within hours of the vulnerabilities being published, according to analysis from Cloudflare—unsurprising given broad access to AI tools that can make it easier for attackers to quickly exploit flaws.

items.title: Drizz's AI App Testing Ambition Meets Reality
items.summary: Mobile app testing is often a race against change. A redesigned screen, a renamed button or an unexpected pop-up can break an automated test, forcing developers to spend time fixing scripts instead of testing functionality. Bengaluru-based Drizz wants AI to make that process less brittle. Its agent, Fathom, uses visual models to interpret app screens and execute tests from natural-language instructions, rather than relying solely on predefined element identifiers.

items.title: Moonshot AI launches new flagship Kim K3.1 Pro model with 3T parameters
items.summary: Moonshot AI today introduced Kim K3.1 Pro, a large language model that can perform some tasks better than Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The LLM is a post-trained, or upgraded, version of an algorithm that the Chinese artificial intelligence company released in July. The latter model, Kimi K3, comprises 896 individual neural networks with 3 trillion parameters. It only activates 16 of those neural networks at any given time to minimize inference costs.
